correctness.rationale: For a!=0, all real b, direct cancellation in H=z+x/a gives Hdot=1-b*z. When b=0, on radius R the bound |H|<=R*sqrt(1+a^-2) and Hdot=1 give T<=2R*sqrt(1+a^-2). For b!=0 equilibrium E_b=(-b^-2,0,b^-1) has radius sqrt(b^-4+b^-2). If a length-T trajectory resides below this radius, time averages give |zbar-1/b|<=2K/(|b|T) and |zbar^2-b^-2|<=4K(1+K)/(b^2 T) for T>=1, while ydot=x+z^2 and Jensen imply xbar<=-b^-2+(C+2R)/T; a second Jensen bound yields R^2>=b^-4+b^-2-(2LD+C)/T once T>=2D/L. Thus all below-radius residence times admit uniform upper bounds, whereas equilibrium yields unbounded length at or above radius. Invariant measures have E[z|H]=1/b via arbitrary smooth test functions, E[x]=-b^-2-Var(z), Cov(x,z)=-a Var(z) and exact radial expectation L^2+L+(2L+1)v+v^2+Var(x)+E y^2. If v=0 invariance enforces the unique equilibrium; any other state straddles its z-height. Independent SymPy check Hdot identity and radius substitution; checked numerical bounds algebra. This is about trajectory *segments*, not all escaping solutions.

value.rationale: An origin-centered exact radius necessary and sufficient for arbitrarily long residence is a natural dynamical invariant of the canonical Sprott N flow. The explicit uniform time bound distinguishes prolonged chaotic-looking transients from possible compact recurrence; the height-conditioned stationarity and strict radial defect add meaningful infinite-time statistics beyond a trivial equilibrium existence calculation. The parameter b=0 boundary is separately sharp. No broader attractor classification is claimed.
